institution: Buck Institute for Research on Aging

key_people.name: Gordon Lithgow
key_people.role: C. elegans geroscience, chief academic officer

focus: Geroscience: cellular senescence/SASP, NAD+ metabolism, proteostasis, model-organism lifespan. The first US institute dedicated solely to aging biology.
notable_output: SASP (senescence-associated secretory phenotype) characterization (Campisi); senolytics rationale; the geroscience hypothesis (Kennedy/Kaeberlein 2014, Cell).
funding: NIA grants, philanthropy, Larry Ellison Medical Foundation legacy; ~$60M endowment-era founding gift from Buck Trust.
notes: Anchor academic-nonprofit node of the geroscience field.

focus: Circadian/metabolic biology, partial epigenetic reprogramming, mitochondrial aging.
notable_output: Ocampo et al. 2016 Cell (in-vivo partial reprogramming extends lifespan in progeroid mice); Panda time-restricted feeding mouse work.
funding: NIH/NIA, NSF, private philanthropy.
notes: Reprogramming work seeded Altos Labs hiring (Izpisua Belmonte).

key_people.name: David Sinclair
key_people.role: sirtuins, NAD+, information theory of aging (frontier-contested)

key_people.name: Vadim Gladyshev
key_people.role: comparative biology of aging, redox, aging clocks

focus: Sirtuin/NAD+ biology, epigenetic clocks & reprogramming, comparative genomics of lifespan, gene therapy.
notable_output: Lu et al. 2020 Nature (OSK reprogramming restores vision in mice); sirtuin activation literature (contested); Gladyshev pan-mammalian methylation clocks.
funding: NIH/NIA, HHMI, Glenn Foundation for Medical Research (Paul F. Glenn Center at HMS), industry sponsorships.
notes: Sinclair's claims carry COI/hype flags; grade primary sources, not the spokesperson.

key_people.name: Tony Wyss-Coray
key_people.role: young plasma, parabiosis, brain aging, organ aging clocks

focus: Systemic factors of aging (young vs old plasma), brain aging, plasma-proteomic 'organ age' clocks.
notable_output: Villeda/Wyss-Coray heterochronic parabiosis cognition studies (Nature 2011/2014); organ-specific aging clocks from plasma proteomics (Nature 2023).
funding: NIA, NOMIS Foundation, Alkahest (spinout) partnership.
notes: Spawned Alkahest (plasma-fraction therapeutics).

key_people.name: Matt Kaeberlein
key_people.role: rapamycin/mTOR, Dog Aging Project (left UW 2023 → Optispan)

focus: mTOR/rapamycin geroscience and companion-dog aging (Kaeberlein); structured/EZ water biophysics (Pollack — bridges to bucket-canon biophysics).
notable_output: Dog Aging Project + TRIAD rapamycin companion-dog trial; Pollack 'The Fourth Phase of Water' (2013).
funding: NIA U19 (Dog Aging Project, ~$23M), Glenn Foundation; Pollack work largely independently/privately funded.
notes: Kaeberlein now runs Optispan (industry) but UW remains the Dog Aging Project home; Pollack's EZ-water is a fringe-to-canon biophysics node.

key_people.name: Irina Conboy
key_people.role: heterochronic parabiosis, blood dilution / plasma exchange

focus: Heterochronic parabiosis, stem-cell aging reversibility, neutral blood exchange (TPE) as a rejuvenation lever.
notable_output: Conboy et al. 2005 Nature (young systemic environment rejuvenates old stem cells); 2020 blood-dilution / plasma-exchange reframing of parabiosis.
funding: NIH/NIA, CIRM (California stem-cell agency).
notes: Conboy reframes 'young blood' benefit as dilution of old pro-aging factors, not addition of youth factors — a live conflict with the GDF11/Wagers camp.

institution: Tufts University (Levin / Allen Discovery Center; HNRCA; CALERIE coordinating site)

key_people.name: Michael Levin
key_people.role: bioelectricity, morphogenetic fields, regeneration (bridges to bucket-canon biophysics)

focus: Bioelectric control of growth/regeneration & morphogenesis (Levin); human caloric-restriction biology (HNRCA, CALERIE coordinating center).
notable_output: Levin xenobots and bioelectric pattern-control work; CALERIE Legacy Study (NCT05651620) tracking long-term biological-age effects of 2-year CR.
funding: NIA (CALERIE), Allen Discovery Center / Paul G. Allen Frontiers Group (Levin), Astera/Templeton (Levin).
notes: Levin is a fringe-to-canon biophysics figure (per Becker/Levin in the ideal-state map A-branch); CALERIE is the landmark human CR program.

institution: Albert Einstein College of Medicine (Institute for Aging Research)
focus: Centenarian/longevity genetics (Longevity Genes Project, Ashkenazi cohort), metformin as a geroprotector, autophagy.
notable_output: TAME (Targeting Aging with Metformin) trial design & advocacy; centenarian CETP/IGF-1/APOC3 longevity-gene findings; Cuervo CMA mechanism.
funding: NIA, AFAR (American Federation for Aging Research, which administers TAME), Glenn Foundation, philanthropy. TAME (~$75M target) chronically underfunded.
notes: Barzilai/TAME is the field's bid for an FDA 'aging-as-indication' precedent; trial still not fully funded/launched as of 2026.

institution: USC Leonard Davis School of Gerontology (Longevity Institute)
focus: Dietary/fasting interventions, IGF-1/GH axis, fasting-mimicking diet (FMD), nutrition-longevity translation.
notable_output: Fasting-mimicking diet protocol & human trials; Laron-syndrome (GHR deficiency) cancer/diabetes protection cohort; 'The Longevity Diet'.
funding: NIA, NCI; Longo COI: founder of L-Nutra (ProLon) — donates equity to charity per his statements.
notes: Longo COI (ProLon/L-Nutra) is documented; champions the high-protein-shortens-lifespan side of the protein/mTOR conflict.

location: San Diego / Bay Area / Cambridge UK
focus: Cellular rejuvenation programming (partial Yamanaka-factor reprogramming) to restore cell health and reverse disease.
notable_output: Largest-ever biotech launch (~$3B initial funding, 2022); recruited star reprogramming/clock scientists.
funding: ~$3B private (reported backers include Jeff Bezos and Yuri Milner). No public product yet.
notes: Pulled academic talent (Belmonte/Salk, Levine/Yale, Horvath/UCLA) into industry; reprogramming-centric thesis.

key_people.name: Cynthia Kenyon
key_people.role: VP Aging Research; daf-2/IGF lifespan pioneer

focus: Basic biology of aging and lifespan; naked mole-rat & comparative biology; computational/genomic discovery. Famously secretive.
notable_output: Naked mole-rat non-aging mortality data (Ruby et al. 2018, eLife); AbbVie drug-development partnership.
funding: Alphabet (Google) + AbbVie, ~$2.5B committed. Little public clinical output after 10+ years — a cautionary data point.
notes: OpenAlex shows ~0 indexed works under the company entity (publishes via partners/affiliations); long-horizon, low-disclosure model.

focus: Cellular reprogramming, autophagy, and plasma-fraction approaches to add 10 years to human healthy lifespan.
notable_output: Launched 2022 with $180M, reportedly funded substantially by Sam Altman ($180M personal). Early-stage.
funding: ~$180M (Sam Altman). Private.
notes: Not meaningfully indexed in OpenAlex (private, early). Reprogramming + autophagy + young-plasma thesis.

focus: Epigenetic reprogramming guided by machine learning to restore youthful gene-expression in specific cell types (hepatocytes, T cells).
notable_output: Published preprints on ML-discovered reprogramming factor combinations; $130M Series A (2024).
funding: ~$110M+ initial (Brian Armstrong), $130M Series A led by Kleiner Perkins.
notes: ML-first reprogramming-factor discovery; publishes more openly than most peers.

focus: Human-data-driven drug discovery using longitudinal aging biobanks to find targets; metabolic aging & muscle (apelin/NLRP3 pathways), now obesity/metabolic.
notable_output: IPO'd 2024; lead program azelaprag (apelin agonist) for muscle preservation with GLP-1s (program setbacks 2024). Aging-biobank target-discovery platform.
funding: Public (IPO ~$200M+, 2024); prior VC (Andreessen Horowitz, others).
notes: Pivoted toward metabolic/obesity-adjacent indications (the GLP-1 longevity-overlap thread).

focus: Senolytics — selectively clearing senescent cells. Pivoted from osteoarthritis (UBX0101 failed Ph2, 2020) to ophthalmology (UBX1325/foselutoclax for diabetic macular edema).
notable_output: First senolytics company to go public (2018); UBX0101 knee-OA Phase 2 failure is a key negative datapoint for systemic senolytics hype; UBX1325 eye program ongoing.
funding: Public; backers included ARCH, Venrock, Jeff Bezos, Peter Thiel.
notes: The cautionary senolytics case: strong mouse data (van Deursen p16-clearance, Nature 2011/2016) did NOT translate to the first human joint trial.

focus: Drugs to extend healthy lifespan in dogs (LOY-001/003 large-breed via IGF-1 reduction; LOY-002 senior dogs via metabolic).
notable_output: First company to receive FDA Center for Veterinary Medicine 'reasonable expectation of effectiveness' for a canine lifespan-extension drug (2023) — a regulatory first for aging-as-indication.
funding: ~$150M+ VC (Khosla, First Round, others).
notes: Dog longevity is the realistic near-term regulatory wedge for 'aging as a treatable indication.' IGF-1 axis ties to Bartke/Barzilai biology.

focus: Physics-of-aging modeling — dynamic biomarkers of aging, resilience/recovery rate from biobank time-series, target discovery from the 'aging as loss of resilience' framework.
notable_output: Pyrkov/Fedichev 2021 Nat Commun: human dynamic-organism-state-indicator (DOSI) implies an absolute ~120-150 yr limit from loss of resilience; partnership with Pfizer.
funding: VC; pharma partnerships (Pfizer).
notes: Physics/dynamical-systems framing of aging — bridges to bucket-canon (resilience as a measurable order parameter).

focus: Portfolio/pipeline company for senescence, regeneration, and aging-associated disease therapeutics.
notable_output: Multiple programs (e.g., RJx senolytic/anti-fibrotic assets); founded with Max Planck / ETH ties.
funding: VC + strategic (founded with backing including the Max Planck-adjacent ecosystem).
notes: European industry node; less public output than US peers.

institution: SENS Research Foundation / Longevity Escape Velocity (LEV) Foundation

key_people.name: Aubrey de Grey
key_people.role: co-founder SENS; founder & president, LEV Foundation

focus: Damage-repair paradigm of aging (SENS: seven categories of damage). LEV Foundation runs Robust Mouse Rejuvenation (combination interventions in already-old mice).
notable_output: SENS framework (de Grey 2007, 'Ending Aging'); LEV Robust Mouse Rejuvenation Study 1 (rapamycin + senolytics + HSC + plasma combos), results emerging.
funding: Philanthropy (crypto donors incl. Vitalik Buterin to SENS; de Grey's inherited bequest). De Grey left SENS 2021 amid governance controversy, founded LEV.
notes: Frontier-contested; the damage-repair 'engineering' paradigm vs the mainstream geroscience 'slow the rate' paradigm is a foundational framing conflict.

focus: Incentive prizes and seed funding for regenerative/longevity science.
notable_output: Mprize (Methuselah Mouse Prize) for mouse-longevity records; New Organ Prize; early funder of Organovo, Oisin, Leucadia, Viscient.
funding: Philanthropy; revolving venture-philanthropy model (reinvests exits).
notes: The original prize-driven catalyst of modern longevity philanthropy (Mprize, 2003).

focus: Largest-ever dedicated healthspan funder — grants and venture investment in geroscience worldwide. Pledged up to ~$1B/year.
notable_output: Hevolution-AFAR New Investigator awards; co-funds TAME-adjacent work; Geroscience grant program.
funding: Saudi sovereign / royal backing (PIF-adjacent), targeting ~$1B/yr deployment.
notes: Single most significant new funding source in the field (since ~2021); reshapes who gets funded globally.

focus: High-risk 'open science' bets and Focused Research Organizations (FROs); funds metascience, neuro, and some aging/biology moonshots.
notable_output: Backs FROs and open-science infrastructure; funder adjacent to Levin-style frontier biology.
funding: Jed McCaleb personal philanthropy.
notes: Mechanism-design funder (FRO model) rather than a bench lab.

focus: Fast, low-bureaucracy grants for aging biology research (modeled on Fast Grants). Funds high-risk early geroscience.
notable_output: Rapid 'apply in a weekend' aging-research grants (~$25M+ deployed since 2021).
funding: Philanthropy (Vitalik Buterin, Open Philanthropy, Jaan Tallinn, others); operated with Norn Group / Patrick Collison-adjacent metascience ethos.
notes: Speed-of-funding experiment; lowers activation energy for unconventional aging projects.

focus: Largest public funder of aging research; runs the Interventions Testing Program (ITP), Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging (BLSA), and most US geroscience grants.
notable_output: NIA Interventions Testing Program (ITP) — the gold-standard multi-site mouse-lifespan testbed that validated rapamycin, acarbose, 17-α-estradiol, canagliflozin; BLSA; funds CALERIE, Dog Aging Project, much of the field.
funding: US federal appropriation (~$4.5B/yr, the majority earmarked for Alzheimer's by Congress).
notes: The ITP is the field's quality filter (Richard Miller / Strong / Harrison) — separates real geroprotectors from hype. Funding skewed to Alzheimer's by congressional mandate.
